Polynomial Algebra of Observed Derivatives

Source: R/dexpected_method.R
dexpected_poly.Rd

Helpers for the derivatives of the expected-information matrix under an explicit method. A polynomial is a list of terms, each a list with a numeric coef and f, a list of sorted integer index tuples, one per factor \(\ell_T\).

Usage

poly_base(identity, a, b)

poly_d(poly, cc, moved)

poly_order(poly)

poly_eval(poly, getter)

Arguments

identity

"hessian" or "score".

a, b

Parameter indices of the pair.

poly

A polynomial.

cc

The index of the differentiating parameter.

moved

Whether the density moves with the parameter.

getter

A function of a sorted index tuple returning the observed derivative, a numeric vector.

Value

poly_base() and poly_d() return a polynomial, poly_order() an integer and poly_eval() a numeric vector.

Details

poly_base() returns the integrand of the identity for the pair \((a,b)\): \(\ell_{ab}\) for "hessian" and \(-\ell_a\ell_b\) for "score". poly_d() applies the derivative with respect to the parameter cc: the Leibniz derivative, which replaces each factor \(\ell_T\) by \(\ell_{T\cup c}\), and, when moved is TRUE, also the term \(f\,\ell_c\) that comes from the density. poly_order() is the largest derivative order that appears, and poly_eval() evaluates the polynomial with a function that returns the observed derivative of a tuple.

See also

dexpected_by_method()
